Note: HEURISTIC, NOT AUTHORITATIVE. Microsoft's own DeviceEvents table reference explicitly states that the full set of ActionType values is only available via 'the built-in schema reference available in the Defender portal' -- there is no publicly published, exhaustive list of exact ActionType strings for automated response/containment/remediation actions (device isolation, file quarantine, etc.). The one specific, confirmed fact found during research: Microsoft's own documentation for investigating response actions says to 'look for any action type starting with contain in the DeviceEvents table' for containment actions. Everything else in this list is a substring-match heuristic built from the general vocabulary Microsoft uses when describing these actions in its documentation (isolate, quarantine, remediate, restrict, block), not confirmed exact ActionType values. This will have both false negatives (a real response action whose ActionType doesn't happen to contain any of these substrings) and, more rarely, false positives (an unrelated ActionType that happens to contain one of these substrings). An analyst with access to their own tenant's Defender portal schema reference should override DefaultKeywords via Invoke-MDEDetection's -ResponseActionKeywords parameter with their environment's exact ActionType values whenever precision matters -- this file's list is a starting point for a best-effort estimate, not a substitute for that.
